Name: Shadow Shaman is Paracas Iconography
Author: aylen13tejas
Description:
Remade the Shadow Shaman's mask taking inspiration from ancient Paracas iconography.

The Paracas Culture was an important society in the history of Peru, well known for its textile art, mummies, and the practice of cranial trepanation used to treat fractures and tumors of the skull. It emerged approximately between 700 BC and AD 200. The Paracas developed on the Paracas Peninsula, located in what is now the district of Paracas in the province of Pisco, in the Ica Region, about 18 kilometers from the city of Pisco, on the southern coast of Peru [url=https://historiaperuana.pe/periodo-autoctono/cultura-paracas][1][/url].

The icon I got the inspiration from was found in a Paracas mantle. [url=https://www.fondoeditorialbcp.com/assets/pdf/ARTE-PRECOLOMBINO-PRIMERA-PARTE-TEXTIL-Y-ADORNOS.pdf][/url]
Technique: embroidery, looping, and fringe work.
Border and central field decorated with diagonally arranged anthropomorphic figures. The central field features alternating anthropomorphic figures wearing shoulder capes and [i]anacos[/i] (traditional garments). The faces display nose ornaments or masks that divide the visage into two sections. In their hands, the figures carry trophy heads and staffs.  [url=https://www.fondoeditorialbcp.com/assets/pdf/ARTE-PRECOLOMBINO-PRIMERA-PARTE-TEXTIL-Y-ADORNOS.pdf][2][/url]
